wellness.hero_subtitle: Check in whenever the mood shifts. Everything here stays on this device.
wellness.checkin_sub: Tap the face that fits this moment
wellness.cbt_sub: A short, guided exercise based on your last check-in
wellness.cbt_idle_sub: I will pick an exercise that matches how you last felt.
wellness.cbt_idle_no_entry: Log a mood first, and I will suggest an exercise that fits it.
wellness.cbt_disclaimer: These exercises are self-help guidance, not medical advice. If you are in distress or thinking about harming yourself, please contact a local health professional or emergency service.
wellness.cbt_tone_low: That sounds heavy, and it makes sense that it is hard right now. Let us take one small step together rather than fixing everything at once.
wellness.cbt_tone_mixed: It sounds like a mixed stretch — some of it fine, some of it not. That is worth taking seriously either way.
wellness.cbt_tone_steady: A steady day is a real result, not a nothing day. Let us keep a little of that steadiness for tomorrow.
wellness.cbt_tone_bright: Good to hear things feel lighter. Noticing what helped is what makes it repeatable.
wellness.cbt_reframe_step_1: Write down the exact thought that keeps returning, in the words you actually use.
wellness.cbt_reframe_step_2: List one piece of evidence for it and one against it. Just one each is enough.
wellness.cbt_reframe_step_3: Rewrite the thought so it stays true but fits both pieces of evidence.
wellness.cbt_reframe_prompt: If a friend said this thought out loud, what would you answer them?
wellness.cbt_grounding_step_1: Put both feet flat on the floor and notice the weight of your body on the chair.
wellness.cbt_grounding_step_2: Name five things you can see, four you can hear, and three you can touch.
wellness.cbt_grounding_step_3: Say the date and where you are, out loud or silently.
wellness.cbt_grounding_prompt: What is one thing in this room that is genuinely safe right now?
wellness.cbt_breathing_step_1: Breathe in through your nose for a count of four.
wellness.cbt_breathing_step_2: Hold gently for four, then breathe out for six.
wellness.cbt_breathing_step_3: Repeat six times, letting the out-breath stay longer than the in-breath.
wellness.cbt_breathing_prompt: What is different in your shoulders and jaw now compared with a minute ago?
wellness.cbt_gratitude_step_1: Name one thing today that went the way you hoped, however small.
wellness.cbt_gratitude_step_2: Name one person who made the day easier, and how.
wellness.cbt_gratitude_step_3: Name one thing you did yourself that you would not want overlooked.
wellness.cbt_gratitude_prompt: Which of those three is worth carrying into tomorrow?
wellness.med_sub: Structured sessions you can follow without sound or a connection
wellness.med_note: Move at your own pace. Stopping early is fine — a short session you finish is worth more than a long one you dread.
wellness.med_box_breath_sub: An even, four-count rhythm for when the body is running faster than the situation needs.
wellness.med_box_breath_step_1: Sit upright, rest your hands, and let your eyes close or soften.
wellness.med_box_breath_step_2: Breathe in for four counts, hold for four.
wellness.med_box_breath_step_3: Breathe out for four counts, hold empty for four.
wellness.med_box_breath_step_4: Continue for sixteen rounds, then sit still for a moment before moving.
wellness.med_body_scan_sub: A slow pass from head to feet, releasing what has quietly tightened during the day.
wellness.med_body_scan_step_1: Lie down or sit back, and take three unhurried breaths.
wellness.med_body_scan_step_2: Bring attention to your scalp, face and jaw, and let each soften as you exhale.
wellness.med_body_scan_step_3: Move down through shoulders, arms, chest, stomach, hips and legs, pausing at each.
wellness.med_body_scan_step_4: Finish at your feet, then notice the whole body at once for a final minute.
wellness.med_wind_down_sub: A ten-minute close to the day, for a mind that keeps working after the lights go off.
wellness.med_wind_down_step_1: Put the phone face down and dim the light in the room.
wellness.med_wind_down_step_2: Breathe out slowly five times, longer out than in.
wellness.med_wind_down_step_3: Name three things from today you are setting down until tomorrow.
wellness.med_wind_down_step_4: Rest attention on the weight of the blanket or the sound of the room, and let it stay there.
wellness.med_focus_reset_sub: A short reset between tasks, for when attention has scattered but the day is not over.
wellness.med_focus_reset_step_1: Stop what you are doing and sit back from the screen.
wellness.med_focus_reset_step_2: For one minute, notice what you are feeling without changing it.
wellness.med_focus_reset_step_3: For one minute, follow the breath in and out.
wellness.med_focus_reset_step_4: For one minute, widen attention to the whole body, then choose the one next thing.
wellness.history_sub: Tap an entry to edit or remove it
wellness.empty_sub: Log how you feel once, and the trend and coaching will start working from it.
wellness.delete_confirm_msg: This check-in will be removed from your history and from the 7-day trend.
wellness.privacy_note: Mood entries are stored only on this device. They are not shared with your family group and are never uploaded.

cycle.hero_no_data_sub: Log one period and predictions begin from there
cycle.stage_sub: This changes what is predicted and which guidance is shown
cycle.stage_cycling_desc: Ordinary cycle tracking, with predictions for your next period, ovulation and fertile window.
cycle.stage_cycling_nutrition_1: Keep iron up around your period — lentils, dark greens, and meat or fish if you eat them.
cycle.stage_cycling_nutrition_2: Pair iron-rich food with vitamin C, such as lemon or amla, to absorb more of it.
cycle.stage_cycling_nutrition_3: Steady the luteal-phase energy dip with complex carbohydrates rather than quick sugar.
cycle.stage_cycling_exercise_1: Keep heavier training for the week after your period, when energy usually peaks.
cycle.stage_cycling_exercise_2: Swap intensity for walking, yoga or stretching on the heaviest days.
cycle.stage_cycling_exercise_3: Track how each phase feels for two cycles before changing your routine.
cycle.stage_fertility_desc: Planning for pregnancy. The fertile window and ovulation estimate are highlighted, with a reminder before the window opens.
cycle.stage_fertility_nutrition_1: Take folate daily, ideally from before conception, on medical advice.
cycle.stage_fertility_nutrition_2: Include whole grains, pulses and healthy fats; keep alcohol and heavy caffeine low.
cycle.stage_fertility_nutrition_3: Ask a doctor about vitamin D and B12 rather than guessing at supplements.
cycle.stage_fertility_exercise_1: Moderate activity most days supports fertility better than long, intense sessions.
cycle.stage_fertility_exercise_2: Strength work twice a week helps insulin sensitivity, which matters for ovulation.
cycle.stage_fertility_exercise_3: Protect sleep and manage stress — both affect cycles as much as training does.
cycle.stage_postpartum_desc: Recovery after birth. Cycles often return late and irregularly, especially while breastfeeding, so predictions stay deliberately cautious.
cycle.stage_postpartum_nutrition_1: Eat regularly and drink more than usual, particularly if you are breastfeeding.
cycle.stage_postpartum_nutrition_2: Keep protein, iron and calcium up while your body rebuilds its stores.
cycle.stage_postpartum_nutrition_3: Continue any prescribed supplements until your doctor says otherwise.
cycle.stage_postpartum_exercise_1: Start with walking and breathing work, and get clearance before anything heavier.
cycle.stage_postpartum_exercise_2: Rebuild the pelvic floor and deep abdominal muscles before returning to impact.
cycle.stage_postpartum_exercise_3: Stop and ask for advice if you notice leaking, pain or a gap along the midline.
cycle.stage_perimenopause_desc: The years before periods stop, when cycles get shorter, longer or skip entirely. Predictions here are indicative only.
cycle.stage_perimenopause_nutrition_1: Prioritise calcium and vitamin D — bone loss speeds up in this stage.
cycle.stage_perimenopause_nutrition_2: Keep protein at every meal to hold on to muscle.
cycle.stage_perimenopause_nutrition_3: Notice whether caffeine, alcohol or spice trigger hot flushes for you, and adjust.
cycle.stage_perimenopause_exercise_1: Strength training twice a week protects bone density and muscle.
cycle.stage_perimenopause_exercise_2: Add weight-bearing movement such as brisk walking or stair climbing.
cycle.stage_perimenopause_exercise_3: Balance work now reduces fall risk considerably later.
cycle.stage_menopause_desc: Twelve months or more without a period. Cycle prediction is switched off, and the focus moves to symptoms, bone health and long-term wellbeing.
cycle.stage_menopause_nutrition_1: Keep calcium and vitamin D consistent, and have levels checked periodically.
cycle.stage_menopause_nutrition_2: Fibre and healthy fats support heart health, which needs more attention after menopause.
cycle.stage_menopause_nutrition_3: Watch portion drift rather than dieting — metabolism shifts gradually, not overnight.
cycle.stage_menopause_exercise_1: Keep strength training twice a week; it is the single most protective habit here.
cycle.stage_menopause_exercise_2: Aim for regular moderate cardio for heart and mood.
cycle.stage_menopause_exercise_3: Yoga or stretching helps with stiffness and sleep quality.
cycle.prediction_sub: Estimated from the periods you have logged
cycle.prediction_disclaimer: These are estimates from your own logged dates, not a medical assessment, and they are not reliable as contraception.
cycle.prediction_empty_sub: Log the first day of your last period and an estimate appears immediately, sharpening with each cycle you add.
cycle.prediction_menopause_sub: You have set your life stage to menopause, so no next period is predicted. Symptom logging and guidance stay available.
cycle.reminders_sub: What you would be alerted about, based on today
cycle.reminders_pending_note: Shown inside the app for now. Phone notifications arrive once the app's reminder system is added.
cycle.reminders_empty: Nothing coming up in the next few days.
cycle.reminder_log_open_period: Add an end date to your current period
cycle.history_sub: Tap an entry to edit or remove it
cycle.empty_sub: Add the first day of your most recent period to begin.
cycle.entry_ongoing: Still ongoing — add an end date when it finishes
cycle.placeholder_end: Leave empty if it is still ongoing
cycle.end_hint: Use the − and + buttons to move a day at a time, or type the date directly.
cycle.delete_confirm_msg: This entry will be removed, and your average cycle length will be recalculated without it.
cycle.invalid_start_msg: Enter the first day as a real date in YYYY-MM-DD format.
cycle.invalid_end_msg: The last day must be a real date in YYYY-MM-DD format, and cannot come before the first day.
cycle.invalid_cycle_length_msg: Enter a typical cycle length between 15 and 60 days.
cycle.invalid_period_length_msg: Enter a typical period length between 1 and 14 days.
cycle.duplicate_msg: A period starting on that date is already logged.
cycle.settings_sub: Used until you have logged enough cycles for your own averages to take over.
